This message comes from Capital One with the Venture X Card.
Earn unlimited double miles and a $300 annual Capital One travel credit.
Capital One.
What's in your wallet?
Terms of fly.
Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
More than 56 million people have already voted early in this year's midterm elections, according
to the University of Florida's Election Lab and Piers Tamara Keith with more.
This election season started out on favorable ground for Republicans, between a Senate map
that runs through red states and all the gerrymandering of House districts.
But voters are unhappy.
The average price of regular gasoline is over $4 a gallon.
Inflation is up.
People are worried about artificial intelligence and data centers.
The war with Iran is unpopular, and voters are increasingly voicing concerns about corruption.
Senate races in deep red Republican territory are competitive, as are House districts where
President Trump won by 10 points or more just two years ago.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
In Michigan, defeated primary candidate Haley Stevens is persona non grata in the Democratic
Party.
She has seriously hurt herself in the Democratic Party, and probably there is not a place for
her right now.
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell, speaking to NPR's Morning Edition, a day after Stevens
stunned members of her party by endorsing Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers instead
of her own party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed, in a close and consequential race for control
of Congress.
Dingell said she spoke with Stevens over the weekend and was under the impression Stevens
would back the party nominee.
In an interview with CNN's Anderson Cooper, Stevens was pressed on what specifically prompted
the sudden shift but repeatedly declined to offer a direct answer.
The Department of Justice is asking the Supreme Court to wade into its feud with California
over the state's voter rolls.
The Justice Department filed a notice on the eve of the midterm elections after a federal
district judge and a divided Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals panel declined to order California
to set aside and stop processing the ballots of thousands of people.
The DOJ alleges it has identified 20,000 likely non-citizens on California's voter rolls whose
ballots should not be counted until their citizenship can be verified.
Federal investigators are expected to update the public today about the business jet that
crashed into a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach, Florida yesterday.
All nine people on board died.
Governor Ron DeSantis says there were no reports of people on the ground killed or injured.
LiveATC.net has air traffic control recordings from the plane that began its flight in Austin,
Texas and was flying east at 35,000 feet, bound for the Bahamas.
The pilot has heard reporting ICE on the jet requesting permission to climb 2,000 feet and
then quickly issuing a May Day in reporting the plane's rapid descent.
Eyewitness recordings show the small aircraft heading to the ground like a missile and exploding
in flames.
It's NPR.
Arab states are urging diplomacy in the wake of a U.S. threat of another attack on Iran
after the midterms.
And Pierre's Eobotrawi reports.
Qatari mediators are working with Iran on a two-day plan that would halt attacks on ships
in the Strait of Hormuz and lay the ground for direct U.S.-Iran talks again.
But some Gulf Air partners have also been told to prepare for powerful U.S. attacks
on Iran soon.
UAE diplomat Anwar Gargash told a security forum in Bahrain that countries here don't
want that.
We don't really want to see another round of confrontation in the region.
Eyobotrawi, NPR News, Manama, Bahrain.
Open enrollment is underway for the Affordable Care Act marketplaces, including healthcare.gov.
NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports the markets lost millions of enrollees last year as the
federal government stopped giving extra money for some people's premiums.
The marketplaces are designed for people who don't qualify for a public program like Medicare
or Medicaid and who don't get health insurance through their jobs.
Enrollment on healthcare.gov, which is run by the federal government and all of the state-run
marketplaces, hit a record of 24 million in 2025.
This year, that number dropped by nearly 3 million.
The Trump administration claims the decline in enrollment is a result of weeding out people
who were ineligible or "fantom enrollees."
Health experts say that it's more likely due to higher costs.
Republicans in Congress declined to extend extra money that kept premiums more affordable.
Open enrollment runs until at least January 15th.
The exact deadline varies by state.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News.

topics.text: Early voting in midterms reaches 56 million, with Republicans facing an unfavorable national mood
Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over her party's Senate nominee
Justice Department asks Supreme Court to intervene in its dispute with California over voter rolls
Business jet crashes into Palm Beach, Florida neighborhood, killing all nine people aboard
Qatari mediators work on plan to halt Iran attacks on Strait of Hormuz ships and restart US-Iran talks
Affordable Care Act marketplace open enrollment begins after enrollment drops nearly 3 million
